source.original_title: 06/07/2026 - Julian Malfregeot x Andrew Musial KFS
source.display_title: 06/07/2026 - Julian Malfregeot x Andrew Musial KFS — Follow Up

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: All right, so Kim, that you spoke to, told me a little about you, so it seems that you're doing a lot.

prospect.name: Julian Malfregeot
prospect.occupation: Director of Sales for a medtech company; works remotely from a home office
prospect.family_status: Married; six-month-old daughter who sleeps well. Wants more children. His wife trains with him and introduced him to macro tracking four years ago. His own parents were older and could not play sport with him.
prospect.training_background: Over a year of kettlebells and calisthenics five days a week following Maximilian Moves' programmes through the Playbook app, having worked through all of them and now repeating. Has used a 40lb kettlebell for every movement since January, including Turkish get-ups, in 45-minute sessions. Counts macros daily, hits 165g protein, takes creatine, drinks a gallon of water. Previously trained traditional split-style gym sessions and played sports his whole life; now plays tennis only. Found Trevor because Maximilian Moves and Trevor follow each other on Instagram.
prospect.medical: No serious injuries — asked and explicitly denied. Chronic lower back tightness and thigh/glute inflexibility, worse after sitting and after returning to tennis. Completed a three-month chiropractor and physiotherapist programme that helped by strengthening deep core musculature, but has drifted from it. Holds a monthly massage membership.

signals: Textbook case of the defining criterion: anchored to a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked. 'I think I could do Max's program for account macros and just keep going up in kettlebell weight and be fine forever.'
Highly self-directed and capable — a year of consistent five-day-a-week training, disciplined macro tracking, and progression to a 40lb bell on every movement without any coach.

Explicitly ran the ROI calculation and refused on value, not capacity: 'ROI for ROI on this for 6k would just be out, out of my range' and '4K in the market right now could be 5-6K in the same amount of three months.'
Is himself a sales professional and named the dynamic out loud — 'I'm in sales too, man... I do this all day, every single day' — which made every scripted move visible to him.

Counter-signal for the_optimizer: on profile he is the purest optimizer in the batch — 30, lean at 12-13%, successful, wants good to great. He is classified here as bargain hunter only because price functioned as a hard barrier rather than a quality signal, which the optimizer definition explicitly excludes.

goals.text: Learn new movements and tools beyond his current library — steel mace, sandbag work
Build enough knowledge to write his own programming and eventually train other people
Get stronger and move past a 40lb kettlebell ceiling he has sat at since January
Train kettlebells and calisthenics for the rest of his life and stay capable as long as possible
Be an active father who plays with his daughter and any future children rather than watching from the sideline, unlike his own older parents
Improve flexibility and mobility, which he has never taken seriously
Get from roughly 12-13% body fat down to around 10% for the lean aesthetic he had once before

pains.text: Has exhausted his current programme library and is now repeating workouts with nothing new to progress into
Plateaued on weight — same 40lb kettlebell for every movement for five months
Nobody checks his form; he self-corrects using a mirror while twisting his neck to see
Chronic lower back and posterior chain tightness, aggravated by sitting all day and by returning to tennis
Sits for the majority of the working day in a home office and finds it hard to break away
Cannot picture what competence would look like — could not answer what knowledge level he would need to program for himself

objections.raw_quote: For me personally, I would have a hard time justifying 6K for... For this, and I'm in sales too, man.
objections.rep_response: Correctly diagnosed it as value rather than capacity by asking directly whether the issue was value or funds, then responded by discounting — offering an unlisted three-month tier at $4,000 rather than building value against the incumbent programme.

objections.raw_quote: I kind of got the sense from the questions that, like, Kim was asking me on the intake call that, like, maybe more so suited for people that. Are looking to make like a serious change as opposed to the minuscule things that I'm looking to do.
objections.rep_response: Countered that both types are served and offered a single anecdote about a 57-year-old former D1 soccer player, disclosing that prospect's age, athletic history and engagement to a 38-year-old.

objections.raw_quote: I definitely got to go to my wife and be like, Hey, listen, I might spend four grand on a three month program here.
objections.rep_response: Opened by mocking the objection — 'Come on, man, don't give me the wife objection' — then ran one scripted move, asking whether she would be opposed. Julian said she would not be. The rep did not test permission versus input, did not use the not-a-joint-decision frame, and did not offer the scripted deposit-and-refund on the purchase.

objections.raw_quote: I'm not going to just commit to spending 4K with you here on the first call.
objections.rep_response: Pushed back with 'Why not? You feel good about it' and 'Where's the missing piece you're not telling me?', then proposed a $100 deposit to secure a follow-up call. When that was refused he pushed twice more before accepting a two-day callback.

objections.raw_quote: if this is something that I was, if we were in the same city and we could train together or train in person, this would be like a completely different conversation, but doing something like virtually.
objections.rep_response: Agreed the price would be higher in person — 'That would be totally different price range too' — which conceded the prospect's point that virtual delivery is worth less, and did not defend the value of remote coaching.

tiers.note: Unlisted tier invented live after the price objection — 'for you, three months, it would be 4K'. The rep stated 'usually we don't offer three months for the regular people, because it's not enough time in three months to get them in shape.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structured plan was quoted. Against the $4,000 three-month tier the rep said 'you can even split it into installments or put it on a credit. If you like to use your credit score, that's totally fine.' Separately he asked for a $100 refundable deposit to hold a follow-up call slot.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Refund promised on the $100 booking deposit only, not on the programme — 'If you come in in two days when you're going to schedule, and you're going to be like, look, Andrew, I don't want to do it. My wife told me I'm insane. Fine. We'll just refund it.'

evidence: Ended with an agreed two-day callback window: 'Let me know what are your thoughts in like two days' answered with 'That sounds fair.'

Substantial counter-evidence pointing to lost. He refused a refundable $100 deposit outright — 'I'm not going to do a $100 deposit for a follow-up call' — refused to book a specific slot, and said 'for right now, you know, I'm okay for, at the time, for the time being.'

He reframed the whole thing as future-optional: 'definitely something I can keep in my back pocket for the future if something does change' and 'shoot me a followup in a few months, something like that.'
He never conceded the value case: 'it is steep. It is steep for like a workout program, definitely.'

Confidence is deliberately low. This is closer to a soft no than to a live opportunity, and a reasonable auditor could score it lost; it is recorded as follow_up only because the final exchange re-opened a two-day window.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to send his decision by text within two days. No call scheduled, no deposit taken. He asked to be followed up in a few months if nothing changes sooner.

notable.note: Two invented prices on one call. A three-month tier at $4,000 was created live in response to the price objection, and a $100 deposit was requested simply to book a follow-up call, justified by a demand claim from a rep with no closes. The rep also contradicted himself inside three minutes — 'six months is needed for the full transformation' and then 'everything that I covered in six months is the same in three months' — which is the kind of thing that produces a refund request later. The prospect is a sales director who narrated the process back at him throughout ('I'm in sales too, man'), so every move was visible. The genuinely useful commercial signal is that an advanced, lean, well-funded prospect looked at the offer and concluded it was built for people needing rescue, not for him.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion in both directions. The rep's own questions repeatedly appear under Julian's label — 'Do you actually enjoy calorie counting and weighing everything?' at 00:07:01, 'Do you feel like you have any limitations, any injuries after years of playing sports?' at 00:16:17, and 'Is there anything else that I need to cover with you about that?' at 00:25:29 — while Julian's answers appear under the rep's, including 'I'm only, like, watching myself in the mirror' at 00:21:00 and 'I am a tough cookie' at 00:34:26. The rep also speaks under the label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' but is Andrew Musial per title, folder and his own long-distance hiking references. Roles resolved from content throughout; the pricing exchange around 00:26:51 to 00:30:54 required particular care because the $4,000 offer and the prospect's reaction are attributed to the wrong speakers.
